Applying to the Rivermead Post 16
Applying for Rivermead Post 16
In order to apply for Rivermead's Post 16 Provisions, applicants must have an Education Heath and Care Plan. Applications are made via the Local Authority who will send referrals to Rivermead Post 16. Please check your local offer for further information:
For Medway: Transition the different stages of education | Education support for children and young people with SEND | Medway Council for further information on the application process.
For Kent: Phase transfers for children and young people with SEND - Kent County Council
Rivermead Post 16 offer open evenings in either June (for year 10, following the Year 10 Person Centred Annual Review) or October (at the same time as the Year 11 Person Centred Annual Reviews). These Open Evenings allow prospective learners and their families explore the provision and the education on offer. Details of open evening evenings will be shared with local schools and the Local Authority.
Upon successful completion of the application process the Rivermead will make offers and learners will be supported on their transition to Rivermead post 16.

Information for Parents/Carers
Safeguarding children and child protection
All organisations that work with or come into contact with children should have safeguarding policies and procedures to ensure that every child, regardless of their age, disability, gender reassignment, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation, has a right to equal protection from harm.
Setting up and following good safeguarding policies and procedures means children are safe from adults and other children who might pose a risk. This includes voluntary and community organisations, faith groups, private sector providers, as well as schools, hospitals and sports clubs.
What is safeguarding?
Safeguarding is the action that is taken to promote the welfare of children and protect them from harm.
Child protection is part of the safeguarding process. It focuses on protecting individual children identified as suffering or likely to suffer significant harm. This includes child protection procedures which detail how to respond to concerns about a child.
Report Remove Tool - NSPCC
The NSPCC and the Internet Watch Foundation (IWF) in partnership with Yoti (an age verification platform) have launched Report Remove – a tool to help young people under 18 remove sexual images of themselves online. Report Remove can support young people to report sexual images or video shared online and takes steps to remove it, if it is illegal.
Trying to remove an image or video online can be extremely difficult and upsetting for children and young people. Report Remove provides a child-centred approach to image removal which can be done entirely online, and NSPCC’s Childline service will ensure that the young person is safeguarded throughout the process.
For more information, visit Report Remove and make sure the young people you work with are aware of this important tool.
Worried about a child?
Information, help, support and advice if you are worried about a child in Medway.
If you have concerns that a child or young person living in Medway is suffering from harm please use the following contact details;
Rivermead School Safeguarding Team - safeguarding@rivermeadinclusivetrust.org
Medway Children’s Safeguarding Partnership https://www.medway.gov.uk/mscb/
You can also phone 01634 334 466 or the 24 hour emergency number 03000 419 191.

At Rivermead, we have number of extra-curricular opportunities available before / after school and at lunchtimes.

Pathways at SEN disability sports comp
Pathways class represented Rivermead at a Kent SEN disability sports comp in Ashford on Wednesday October 4th. There were schools from all over Kent and they managed to win medals and certificates for coming 4th out of 8 schools competing. This was most of the learners first experience competing for the school, so hopefully they all gained experience of independence and life experience from this. All learners had fun, behaved well and represented Rivermead well, so please give Pathways a well done, if you see them on your travels.

Parents
Welcome to Rivermead School. It’s a real pleasure to introduce you to our wonderful community and to share a little about what makes Rivermead such a special place to learn, grow and belong.
At Rivermead, our aim is simple: we want every young person to flourish. We are dedicated to supporting each learner as a whole person, academically, socially, and emotionally. We give them the opportunities, confidence and skills they need for the next stage of their journey. We strongly believe that every child matters, whatever their abilities, needs, or starting points. No one is overlooked and no one falls through the net.
Our curriculum, guided by our mission of Support to Succeed, is inclusive, ambitious and carefully planned to build resilience, independence and a love of learning. Alongside this, our therapeutic and pastoral support is central to our work, ensuring that every learner feels understood, valued and ready to succeed. As Ofsted noted in February 2024, “The appropriate therapeutic care, alongside the ambitious academic curriculum on offer, readies them for the next stage of their education.”
Our vision, shared across the Rivermead Inclusive Trust, is to help every learner feel a genuine sense of belonging through positive relationships. We aim to prepare them for adulthood as confident, capable and caring individuals. We want our learners to recognise their own strengths, be proud of who they are, and actively participate in their community.
Our school values guide everything we do:
Be Ambitious – we aim high and take pride in striving for excellence.
Be Connected – we value our relationships with each other and our wider community.
Be Courageous – we show bravery in our learning and choices, even when things feel tough.
Rivermead feels very much like a family. We celebrate every achievement, whether big or small and we want our learners to enjoy coming to school, knowing they will be supported, encouraged and genuinely cared for. Our staff, parents, carers, governors and learners work closely together to create an environment where everyone feels they belong. Thank you for taking the time to explore our school. I hope our website gives you a good sense of who we are and what we stand for. If you would like to know more or arrange a visit, please get in touch with our school office; we would be delighted to welcome you.

Extreme Weather/ Emergencies
Info for parents
What will happen in the event of extreme weather (snow for example)
We want to ensure that in the event of heavy snowfall or extreme weather conditions, adequate measures are in place to enable our school to remain open. It is always the school’s priority to remain open in order to maintain high standards of learning. To this end, our site staff work tirelessly to ensure that the site is safe for pupils, staff and visitors.
Aims
Reduce unnecessary risks
Reduce accidents in the school
Snow Days – Information & Procedures
At Rivermead school, we are aware that the timings of our decisions to close the school are critical for parents and carers, trying to get their children to school and then get to work.
Following a heavy overnight snowfall, we always try and take the judgement on school closure as early as possible in the morning. We aim to make this decision early enough for parents/carers to make alternative plans for childcare or, if there is a heavy snow fall during the day, with enough notice as possible for parents/carers or an alternate to pick up. Whatever the time of day, please be assured that the decision to close the school is taken after considering many factors, particularly the health and safety of our children and staff, and is not taken lightly. The fact that a high proportion of our students are dependent on the buses will also play a part in considerations.
Snowfall Overnight
School Closure
Heavy snowfall overnight may result in access to the school being restricted or may stop children, parents/carers and staff from getting to school safely. If these conditions apply, the following steps will be taken:
Lesson expectations
On the first day of the closure, work will be set via the school website. In the unlikely event that the closure is longer than one day then staff and students will revert to online lessons using Teams in line with our Remote Learning Policy. This will be communicated during day 1.
Delayed opening
In some cases, the snowy conditions on site may just need time to clear or poor local road conditions result in learners or staff taking a longer time to arrive at school. In this case the Headteacher may decide to open the school later or extend the time for registration so that everyone can get to school safely. If the decision for opening later is agreed, following steps will be taken:
Lesson expectations
Work will be set on the school website.
Snowfall during the School Day
In the event of a heavy snowfall and/or there is a significant deterioration in local conditions occurring during the school day, so that the return home may become unsafe, then the Headteacher may decide to close the school. The following procedures will be followed:

Attendance & Absence
Absence from School
Children are required to attend school for 190 days each year. The Government’s target for attendance for Secondary School Pupils is at least 95%.
How does your child’s attendance compare with this target?
The table below indicates how just a few days absence can result in children missing a significant number of lessons. It has been proven that children who miss a lot of school achieve less.

Learner Absence
All absences should be reported to the school office on each day of an absence, unless a long-term absence has been reported. The school attendance officer will contact you either by text message or telephone call if we have not received notification by this time. This contact is to ensure that the student is safe and has not set out from home and failed to arrive at the academy.
When your son/daughter returns could we also ask that you record a note of explanation in their Student Planner.
Holiday Leave
The Department for Education (DfE) are very clear in their expectations of schools and academies that parents or carers should not arrange family holidays during term time. They do, however, recognise that in exceptional circumstances it may be necessary for such holiday leave to be granted. Should you have such a need then your request should be in writing to the Headteacher. You will be notified in writing of the outcome of any such decision.
Please click here to view our Attendance Policy
Covid-19
Please refer to the advice letter sent home to help you make decisions if your child is unwell. If you are unsure then contact school and a member of staff will be able to offer some advice.
The Department for Education coronavirus (COVID-19) helpline is available to answer questions about coronavirus (COVID-19) relating to education and children’s social care. Staff, parents and young people can contact this helpline by calling 0800 046 8687 (Option 1 for a confirmed case)
Monday to Friday from 8am to 6pm. Saturday and Sunday from 10am to 4pm.
